clue.text: Exist as extremely cold people who can't agree?

definitions.text: Exist as extremely cold people who can't agree?

parts.words: Exist as extremely cold people who can't agree?
parts.note: people living at the North and South Poles would be as cold as can be and also as far from each other as possible, which is the idiom for total disagreement

explanation.surface: A wry picture of frozen polar dwellers who never see eye to eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is one cryptic definition: being at opposite poles of the earth is both extremely cold and the image behind the idiom for disagreeing completely.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes two parties with entirely opposed views, so they cannot agree.

clue.text: Yokel hit relations

parts.note: to bump is to hit or knock
kin are one's family relations

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin lashes out at members of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are synonyms for an unsophisticated rustic from the countryside.

clue.text: Examine foreign country, then one relatively prosperous region of ours

parts.note: Peru is a country in South America

parts.words: one relatively prosperous region of ours
parts.note: SE, the South East, is the comparatively wealthy corner of England

explanation.surface: An instruction to study a country abroad and then a well-off part of home.
explanation.walkthrough: SE is the South East of England, around London, regarded as the country's richest region; 'ours' reflects the British setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to look over something carefully, reading or inspecting it in detail.

clue.text: I ask hotel for special arrangement without hesitation

indicators.note: an arrangement made specially reorders the letters of the words I ask hotel

explanation.surface: A guest asks the hotel to make a special booking at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special arrangement' rearranges the letters of I ASK HOTEL; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning immediately or very willingly, as fast as a bullet from a gun.

clue.text: Place offers something worth looking at according to report

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word for a thing worth seeing is taken by its sound

parts.note: a sight is something worth seeing, like a tourist sight

explanation.surface: A location advertised as having an attraction, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a location or spot where something is or happens.

clue.text: It's obvious insect can penetrate banana

indicators.note: one piece getting through into another puts the bug's letters inside the word for obvious

parts.note: plain means clear or obvious
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug can clearly bore its way into a banana.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantain is a kind of starchy cooking banana.

clue.text: Full rent collected by agent, second quarter of the year

indicators.note: rent picked up by the agent follows the agent's letters

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent or representative
to let is to rent out

indicators.note: a four-letter word has four quarters of one letter each, and this takes the second

explanation.surface: A letting agent gathers the full rent in the spring quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second quarter of' the year picks E, the second of the four letters of YEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: filled up completely, often well fed.

clue.text: One animal in a thousand facing terrible peril, bound to be captured

indicators.note: standing in front of, so the thousand comes first

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for a thousand

indicators.note: the leap is held inside the scrambled word for danger
a terrible version is a mangled one, so peril's letters are rearranged

parts.note: a spring is a bound or leap

explanation.surface: One creature in a thousand faces dreadful danger and is sure to be caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' makes LIPER, which 'to be captured' wraps round the leap; 'bound' looks like 'certain' but means a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: The klipspringer is a small African antelope noted for leaping among rocks.

clue.text: See naturalist want to restrict damage

indicators.note: the word for lack holds the damage within it, restricting it

parts.note: want in the sense of lack
to mar is to damage or spoil

explanation.surface: A cross-reference telling the reader to look up a naturalist keen to limit harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' merely introduces the definition, like a reference note; 'want' means lack, not desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck was a French naturalist known for an early theory of evolution.

clue.text: Trudged as little pedestrian behind vehicle

indicators.note: the walker's letters come after the vehicle's

parts.note: a tram is a street vehicle
ped is a short form of pedestrian

explanation.surface: Someone walks wearily, trailing a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: walked heavily and with effort.

clue.text: Evil folk joining renegade, one emerging as anti-establishment figure?

parts.note: demons are evil spirits

indicators.note: the one coming out of the word leaves it shorter

parts.note: a traitor is a renegade
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Wicked people joining a turncoat produce a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emerging' takes I out of TRAITOR to leave TRATOR; the question mark flags a protester as one kind of anti-establishment figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A protester marching against authority is an example of someone opposing the establishment.

clue.text: A king is defeatist ultimately, taking external knock in the country

indicators.note: the inner letters take an outside wrapping from the word for knock

parts.note: to pan is to criticise or knock
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of defeatist

explanation.surface: A defeatist monarch takes a beating from outside in his realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' picks T, the last letter of defeatist; 'knock' means criticise harshly, not strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Pakistan is a country in South Asia.

clue.text: 'Form of water' would be about right

definitions.text: 'Form of water' would be about right

indicators.note: being about something means surrounding it, so the vapour goes round the letter

parts.note: steam is water as vapour

explanation.surface: A quiz-style remark that 'form of water' is the correct description.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue works twice: STEAM placed about R builds the word, and a flowing brook is indeed a form of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook or small river is a body of flowing water.

clue.text: 22 or 25 pounds

definitions.meaning: the answer to 22 across is a nursery word for a horse, and a small horse is another
British slang for twenty-five pounds sterling

explanation.definitionFit: A small horse fits the cross-referenced nursery word, and in London slang the word means twenty-five pounds.

clue.text: Motherly type grabs woman at match, a Scot

indicators.note: the motherly type holds the woman and the a within her letters

parts.note: a hen is a motherly creature, a mother hen
a bride is the woman at a match in the sense of a marriage

explanation.surface: A mother figure clutches a woman at a game, who turns out to be Scottish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests sport but means a marriage, so the woman is a bride.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the Hebrides, the islands off western Scotland, is one kind of Scot.

clue.text: Expression of one's self-confidence after saint appears in big church

indicators.note: the confident phrase follows the saint's name

parts.note: St Basil the Great was an early Church Father
I can is what a confident person says

explanation.surface: A confident remark follows a saint's appearance in a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to or found in a basilica, a large church.

clue.text: A domestic upset undermines school plans

indicators.note: in a down entry, going beneath means following the school's abbreviation
in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, reading them bottom to top

parts.note: domestic animals are tame

explanation.surface: A housemaid's tantrum weakens a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'domestic' looks like a servant but means TAME; 'upset' turns A TAME into EMATA.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of schema, a diagram or outline plan.

clue.text: Jazz fan engaged by certain record companies for shows

indicators.note: the fan is taken on within the record labels' letters

parts.note: indies are independent record labels
cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

explanation.surface: A jazz lover is hired by small record labels to play gigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' looks like a noun for gigs but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: points out or makes evident.

clue.text: Doctor always binding soldiers in extremis — one dealing with wounds

indicators.note: the poetic always wraps round the picked letters

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

indicators.note: in its extremities means the first and last letters of soldiers

explanation.surface: A doctor is forever bandaging soldiers in desperate straits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in extremis' sounds like dire need but takes the ends of soldiers, SS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dresser is a hospital assistant who applies dressings to wounds.

clue.text: Leave out order to get computers, etc

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: An instruction to skip asking for computers and such.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to fail to include or to skip something.

clue.text: Soldiers — stars or bullies?

parts.note: soldiers are men in the ranks
aces are star performers

explanation.surface: Are these troops heroes or thugs?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bullies' reads as a noun but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, both mean threatens or intimidates.

clue.text: Stops and notices five hundred escaping

indicators.note: the numeral getting away drops out of the word for notices

parts.note: adverts are public notices
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Someone halts and spots five hundred breaking free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notices' looks like a verb but is the noun, ADVERTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert is to prevent or ward off, so it stops something happening.

clue.text: Boxer, for instance, showing goodness repeatedly

indicators.note: said again, so the exclamation is doubled

parts.note: gee and goodness are both mild exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A boxer shows good character over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxer is the carthorse in Orwell's Animal Farm, not a fighter or a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's word for a horse, of which Boxer is a famous fictional example.

clue.text: Country is sick, going backwards, old archdeacon admitted

indicators.note: the old archdeacon is let into the reversed letters
the phrase for being ill is read in reverse

parts.note: ails means is ill
Ven, Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A nation is ailing and in decline, with an elderly clergyman taken in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going backwards' turns AILS into SLIA, which 'admitted' opens to take O and VEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenia is a country in central Europe.

clue.text: I paved the way — set up specialist shop

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means written upwards, reversed

parts.note: led means went first or paved the way

explanation.surface: A pioneer boasts of founding a specialist food shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns I LED upward to give the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for delicatessen, a shop selling fine or specialist foods.

clue.text: Take it easy having had meal, say — not for the first time

definitions.text: say — not for the first time

parts.note: to rest is to take it easy
ate means having eaten a meal

explanation.surface: Relax after eating, someone repeats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something again in words is to express it a second time.

clue.text: Island where accountant may be spotted in The Dog and Duck

indicators.note: the accountant is seen inside the dog and duck letters

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
O is a duck, a zero score in cricket
ACA is an Associate Chartered Accountant

explanation.surface: An island where an accountant might be seen in a pub called The Dog and Duck.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dog and Duck is a stock English pub name; here it is CUR and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Curacao is a Caribbean island in the Dutch Antilles.

clue.text: Perverse artistic ones who take Genesis as historical account?

definitions.text: who take Genesis as historical account?

indicators.note: something perverse is contrary or twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Contrary creative types read the Bible's first book literally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perverse' rearranges ARTISTIC ONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Those believers hold that the Bible's account of creation is literal fact.
